headline: A Brookings study of Danish workers found that, up to the end of 2024, chatbots had not changed pay, hours or hiring, but were already changing what workers do.
score_reason: Rigorous, linked-records study and one of the first of its kind; Denmark and data to 2024 limit how far it applies.
importance_line: Workers in AI-exposed jobs have not lost pay or jobs so far, but their tasks are changing and some are switching occupations, though the data end in Dec 2024 and cover only Denmark.
summary: Brookings researchers report that a survey of about 25,000 Danish workers in 11 AI-exposed occupations, linked to official earnings records, shows no effect of chatbot use on pay, hours or hiring up to December 2024, with any difference ruled out above 2%. The study finds work is being reorganised instead: workers report new tasks such as checking AI output, and chatbot users appear more likely to have switched occupations, mostly into IT support and clerical roles.
notes: Published 6 Oct 2026; the data are older (to Dec 2024), stated in the entry.
